Reconcile a statement against its own hierarchy

Source: R/check_statement.R
check_statement.Rd

Checks every subtotal in a tidied statement against the lines below it, and says which of three things is true of each: the reported detail adds up, the statement presents the same figures under two groupings, or there is unspecified detail left over.

Usage

check_statement(x, by = NULL, period = "closing", tol = 1)

Arguments

x

A tibble from add_taxonomy().

by

Columns identifying one statement instance. NULL, the default, uses whichever of file, basis and period the table has – file because read_xbrl() returns many filings at once, and without it two companies with the same balance sheet date are checked as one.

period

"closing", the default, checks the year the filing declares for itself and leaves its comparative out – a comparative is usually partial, and its gaps are not the filing's. NULL checks every period the table carries.

tol

Absolute tolerance in the reporting currency. Default 1.

Value

A tibble with one row per subtotal that has reported detail: the by columns, statement, code, elementid, label, total, specified (the sum of the nearest reported descendants), residual, n_children and verdict.

Children are not one level down

A filer may report a figure while leaving its intermediate parent empty, so the lines that partition a subtotal are the nearest reported descendant on each branch. A fixed depth+1 rule reports discrepancies that are not there.

Debt is presented twice

A Danish balance sheet lists debt both by counterparty and by maturity, so a subtotal's children can hold the same money twice over. When both groupings are complete the children sum to an exact multiple of the subtotal, but they usually are not: one partition is itemised in full while the other is only partly filled in, and the sum lands somewhere in between.

So the test is not a ratio but a search: is there a subset of the children that hits the subtotal exactly? If there is, that subset is a complete grouping and the rest is another view of the same figures. The verdict is "two groupings" and n_partition says how many lines the complete one holds – a presentation feature, named rather than reported as an error.

Repeated lines

The same statement line can arrive more than once – one filing in a sample of 100 reported its cash position six times and its receivables twice, all with the same figure. Repeats that agree are collapsed silently, because nothing turns on them. Repeats that disagree are a different matter: the filing states two different amounts for one line, and the verdict says "conflicting duplicates" rather than quietly keeping whichever came first.

The closing identity

Checking each subtotal against the lines below it never reaches the one identity a statement exists to assert: that assets equal liabilities and equity. Those two are not parent and child but siblings of opposite sign under an abstract root, so they are not summed – they are compared.

The rule needs no list of element names. Where a node's reported children split into a debit group and a credit group, the two must be equal, and the verdict is "sides agree" or "sides differ". In the Danish balance sheet that is exactly Aktiver against Passiver.

The income statement has no such identity: its cascade runs through signed subtotals to Aarets resultat, which is find_signs()'s problem, not a sum.

What an absent line means

The taxonomy offers dozens of alternatives under a subtotal and a company uses a handful. An unreported line means "not applicable", not "unknown", so a residual of zero is the normal and expected result – it says the reported detail already exhausts the subtotal and can be used as it stands.

See also

add_taxonomy(), and find_signs() for the income statement, whose lines carry signs and so are not a plain sum.

Other taxonomy: add_taxonomy(), check_breakdown(), check_cascade(), check_continuity(), check_inclusion(), check_movement(), read_taxonomy(), xbrl_accounts(), xbrl_company(), xbrl_fill(), xbrl_lines(), xbrl_movements(), xbrl_note_tables(), xbrl_period(), xbrl_resolve()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
x <- read_xbrl("materiale/xbrl")
checks <- check_statement(x)
table(checks$verdict)

# what is left unexplained
checks[checks$verdict == "unspecified remainder", ]
} # }
